purpose: Aprepitant is used to prevent nausea and vomiting caused by chemotherapy (cancer treatment). It is also used to prevent nausea and vomiting after surgery. It works best when taken alongside other anti-nausea medicines as part of a combination approach.
how_it_works: Your brain has special receptors that, when triggered, cause the feeling of nausea and vomiting. Aprepitant works by blocking one of those receptors, called the NK1 receptor, so the signal to feel sick is blocked. Think of it like putting a plug in a socket — it stops the 'nausea signal' from getting through.
common_side_effects: Tiredness or weakness, hiccups, constipation or diarrhea, loss of appetite, headache, and dizziness are the most common side effects. Some people may also notice mild stomach upset or heartburn.
warnings: Aprepitant can interact with many other medications, including blood thinners like warfarin, birth control pills (it may make them less effective — use a backup method), and certain other drugs. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines you take. Avoid it if you are taking pimozide. It should be used with caution during pregnancy. Contact your doctor if you develop a severe skin rash or allergic reaction.
typical_dosing: For chemotherapy-related nausea, the usual dose is 125 mg taken by mouth on Day 1 (about 1 hour before chemotherapy), followed by 80 mg once daily on Days 2 and 3. For post-surgery nausea, a single 40 mg dose is taken by mouth within 3 hours before anesthesia. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
